summary: I developed AstroMind, an AI-powered space mission planning suite that combines a deep-space mission planner with MarswalkAI, a NASA data-driven Mars EVA planning tool. The project uses IBM watsonx to help users generate mission profiles, risk assessments, route plans, and formal mission briefs using natural-language AI assistance. It addresses the challenge of making advanced mission planning more accessible, faster, and more iterative for small teams, universities, and emerging space agencies that do not have access to the powerful simulation tools used by large organizations. By integrating NASA mission datasets such as MOLA, CRISM, THEMIS, HiRISE, and MCS into a single browser-based interface, AstroMind helps users evaluate terrain, hazards, science targets, and weather in a unified workflow. This is important because mission planning is complex, time-intensive, and high-risk, and AI-driven decision support can improve safety, efficiency, and mission readiness.
details:
Walid Ibrahim

Date:14/11/2026

Space Exploration

About the Challenge

NASA has explored Mars robotically for decades, studying its extreme environment, mapping its surface, and collecting many types of data. Far from home, the first astronauts to set foot on Mars will want the best map possible, with information on the details of their routes and destinations, updates on current conditions, and the data needed to complete their mission quickly and safely. Your challenge is to create a layered, integrated view of a location or route on the Martian surface that pulls together data from multiple NASA science missions and could help a human explorer plan and carry out a successful Marswalk while conducting new and exciting science along the way.

AstroMind is a browser-based space mission planning suite with two parts: a deep-space mission planner and MarswalkAI, a Mars surface exploration and EVA-planning prototype. Users can choose a destination or landing region, explore mission parameters, and generate AI-assisted plans, hazard assessments, science priorities, timelines, checklists, and mission briefs. MarswalkAI organizes information associated with NASA missions and instruments—including MOLA, CRISM, THEMIS, HiRISE, and Mars rover data—into a single planning interface.

The project aims to make early-stage mission planning more approachable for students, universities, and small teams. Bringing route planning, science objectives, and safety considerations together can help users explore trade-offs and identify risks before a mission is designed in detail. Its intended impact is to support learning and broaden access to space-planning concepts, not replace professional mission analysis.

We built the prototype with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, and designed it to run in a web browser. IBM watsonx.ai (Granite) provides the planned AI reasoning and text-generation integration, and IBM Bob supported development. No specialized hardware is required.

The creative element is combining conversational AI with a visual, layered Mars exploration workflow. We considered usability, accessibility, EVA duration, terrain and environmental hazards, science value, and the need to communicate uncertainty. Note: NASA data values shown in the prototype may be illustrative rather than live data feeds; verify and cite the specific NASA datasets actually used in your submission.
